title: Invertibility of the mixed-universe restricted evaluation mate
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme of universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme] and $U$ any open. Specify the derived categories on $X$ and its over-site with morphism universe $w$ [def-pc-derived-category], and use the standard category on $U.toScheme$ with morphism universe $u+1$. Let $R$ be derived over-site restriction followed by the derived over-equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Write $H_X$ and $H_U$ for the fixed derived internal-Hom functors [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and $e_X,e_U$ for the canonical tensor-Hom bijections [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection], using the recorded derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. For every strong monoidal structure $m$ on $R$ and every $K,N$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, the map $c_{K,N}=e_U^{-1}(\mu_m(H_X(K,N),K);R(e_X(1_{H_X(K,N)})))$ from $R(H_X(K,N))$ to $H_U(RK,RN)$ is an isomorphism. This is pointwise invertibility of an explicitly constructed map; no family of comparisons is chosen and no equation for arbitrary maps into $H_X(K,N)$ is assumed.

proof.text: Obtain J, its adjunction with the specified composite restriction R, and pointwise invertibility of the adjunction-transposed tensor projection morphism from the projection-formula node. Turn each explicit projection morphism into an isomorphism using asIso. Its defining equation follows from adj.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply and homEquiv_unit.

For a test object A, compose five explicit Hom equivalences: the adjunction inverse; canonical e_X at J(A),K,N; precomposition by the projection isomorphism; the adjunction on A tensor R(K),N; and e_U inverse. The private generic mate_isIso_of_projection constructs this equivalence.

Identify that composite with f mapped to f;c. Apply e_U injectivity and expand the Hom equivalence composite. The projection equation, tensor-Hom naturality on X, tensorator naturality, and the adjunction unit equation unit_A;R(q)=f reduce its value to e_U(f;c). This equality is fully proved in the generic private helper.

The explicit equivalence makes postcomposition by c bijective for every test object. Mathlib isIso_of_yoneda_map_bijective proves invertibility of c. This is the entire generic Hom-side argument; no representative or geometric assertion remains in this theorem.

theorem openRestriction_evaluationMate_isIso (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))] :
    let E := (Equivalence.functor
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
      (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    let R := (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ E
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace) X.sheaf
    ∀ m : R.Monoidal,
      letI := m
      ∀ K N : schemeDerivedCategory X,
        IsIso ((schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv U.toScheme
          (R.obj (H.obj (op K, N))) (R.obj K) (R.obj N)).symm
            ((Functor.Monoidal.μIso R (H.obj (op K, N)) K).hom ≫
              R.map (schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv X (H.obj (op K, N)) K N (𝟙 _))))
